title: 1. Two lobes: the rank profile
notes: Colour = c4 (components of rank 4). The two × three map has two separate lobes: c4 = 0 (blue) and c4 ≥ 1 (orange, pink). Almost all new classes are in the c4 = 0 lobe.

title: 2. Where the new classes are
notes: Only new classes and seeds are shown. Compare with the full map (template 1): the new classes fill the high-two side of each lobe; the low-two side is almost all in the catalog.

title: 3. Discovery order × two
notes: x = admission order, y = two. New classes (pink) stay at the top of two for the whole run; the lower band is the c4 ≥ 1 lobe. Look at the change at about id 1.24 million, where generation 2 starts.

title: 4. The frontier moves (playback with a trail)
notes: Plays the admissions from the start; the last 150,000 classes are bright (yellow = newest). Look how the bright part moves to high two and three later in the run.

title: 5. Children fall back to the centre (drift field)
notes: Arrows go from each parent cell to the mean cell of its children. From every side they point to the same centre (two ≈ 380, three ≈ 32): a child does not inherit the position of its parent.

title: 6. Drift of the recent trail only
notes: The same arrows, but only for the last 300,000 admissions. Compare with template 5 to see whether the late search behaves differently.

title: 7. Productive parents (new per million cosets)
notes: Only expanded parents, coloured by new classes per million cosets. Yellow parents are the most efficient; they lie more at high two and high three, but they are few.

title: 8. Yield against 5-spaces
notes: x = maximizing 5-spaces (log), y = new classes reached, for expanded parents. The yield grows with the number of 5-spaces (the work); colour = new per million cosets shows that the efficiency does not.

title: 9. Rediscoveries against two (hubs and open regions)
notes: y = how many paths found each class (log). Classes found many times (hubs) are mostly in the catalog; classes found once or twice are at high two and are more often new.

title: 10. Generations over the order
notes: x = admission order, y = three, colour = generation. Generation 1 (children of the seeds) fills the first 1.24 million ids, then generation 2 starts. The search is breadth-first.

title: 11. du of the ortho-derivative against two
notes: du does not separate new from catalog classes (AUC 0.47), but du = 8 marks a small group of hubs (median 445 rediscoveries). Select one of them to see its lineage.

title: 12. Rare classes: entry four > 0
notes: y = four (entry 4 of the nonbent signature). The 10,319 classes with four > 0 are 49% new and are found less often; they sit at high two and three.

title: 13. Seed families
notes: Colour = the lineage group of the root seed (24 colours). Look whether a family keeps to a region of its own or spreads over the whole map; the drift result suggests that it spreads.
